subject: Oceanography
title: Wind and the Ocean Surface
description: A quick, practical guide to Wind and the Ocean Surface.

hook.text: Wind doesn't just blow over the ocean—it drags the surface water along, creating currents and waves.

buildup.text: Trade winds push tropical water westward—piling it up against continents and driving circulation.

discovery.text: Wind stress also causes upwelling—pulling cold, nutrient-rich water to the surface along certain coasts.

twist.text: The ocean pushes back—warm water heats the air above it, creating winds. It's a two-way conversation.

climax.text: Changes in wind patterns (like weakening trade winds) can trigger El Niño events that reshape global weather.

punchline.text: Wind and ocean are locked in a dance—each leading in turn.

quiz.question: How do winds create ocean currents?
options: Wind drags the surface water along through friction
Wind pushes waves that move water sideways
Wind cools water, making it sink
